campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 1, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered a resolution authorizing an agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority (VTA) to receive Low Carbon Transportation and Operations Program funding for a transit reliability and performance systems project. The agenda also references pothole damage and related claims processes.
keyTopics: Resolution to authorize a fund agreement with VTA for the Low Carbon Transportation and Operations Program
Transit Reliability Improvement and Performance Systems project funding
Pothole damage and the city's claims process

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 2, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council reviewed routine business including meeting minutes, check registers, and the Treasurer's Report, along with draft responses to two county Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole claims and VTA's oversight of BART Silicon Valley Phase II. The Council also considered a transportation impact fee study contract, forming a committee to look at alternative policing services, the future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival, and whether to continue participating in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County.
keyTopics: Draft responses to Civil Grand Jury reports on pothole damage claims and VTA's oversight of BART Silicon Valley Phase II
Support for AB 1761, a bill on data transparency for utility charge calculations
An $85,000 contract with Fehr and Peers for a Transportation Impact Fee study
Forming an Ad-Hoc Committee to review alternative policing services in Saratoga
The future of the Saratoga Blossom Festival and continued city involvement in the Cities Association of Santa Clara County

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 8, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council took up routine budget and contract items, including updated pay schedules for city employee groups and additional funding for an electrical maintenance contractor, alongside a proposal to rename Lee Street to Tubman Street. The Council also discussed committee structures, including changes to the Volunteer Awards Committee and the Environmental Commission, plus a citizen initiative on zoning impacts.
keyTopics: Resolution renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street
Revised Fiscal Year 2026/27 pay schedules for city employee associations and unrepresented staff
Amendment adding $250,000 to the maintenance agreement with Bear Electrical Solutions
Disbanding the joint Los Altos-Los Altos Hills Volunteer Awards Committee to form a Los Altos-only version
Citizen initiative presentation on potential impacts to zoning

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 1, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council reviewed and approved routine meeting minutes from several August 2026 sessions. The Council also considered vacating a public service easement at 15995 Cerro Vista, establishing new preferential and time-limited parking rules, and authorizing a consultant agreement for executive-related services.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from August 10, 17, and 18 Town Council meetings
Resolution to vacate a public service easement at 15995 Cerro Vista
Resolution establishing preferential permit parking and time-limited parking
Consultant agreement for executive services

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 9, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole reviewed the upcoming September 15 and September 22, 2026 City Council agendas, including whether to add items or set specific discussion times. The committee also considered the City Clerk's public record log, the City Auditor's monthly activity report, a mayoral travel request, and a proposal on council transparency and non-disclosure agreements.
keyTopics: Review and finalization of the September 15, 2026 Council agenda
Review of the September 22, 2026 draft Council agenda
Public record log for August 27–September 3, 2026
City Auditor's monthly report of activities for August 2026
Proposal on Council transparency and private non-disclosure agreements

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Council Neighborhoods Committee — September 10, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View Council Neighborhoods Committee held an open session for residents to bring questions and concerns to city staff. Residents were encouraged to submit questions ahead of time online, and staff attended to respond to neighborhood issues raised.
keyTopics: Open Q&A session with city staff on neighborhood concerns
Process for submitting questions in advance via an online form

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 25, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a closed session, a briefing on the Clean Water Program, and a regular meeting covering routine business items like meeting minutes, contracts, and staffing changes. The council also received updates on the Council's Strategic Workplan and Caltrain's budget from a Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board representative.
keyTopics: Clean Water Program update presentation by staff
Purchase order for a new automated materials handling system at the Main Library (up to $635,106.11)
Classification and salary changes for several city job titles, including new manager and coordinator positions
Caltrain budget update from Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board Chief of Staff
Year 1 update on the Council's Strategic Workplan

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — September 9, 2026
cupertino.summary: This meeting kicked off the new term for Cupertino's Teen Commission, starting with the swearing-in of newly appointed commissioners for 2026-2028 and an orientation session. The Commission also reviewed teen program offerings, selected its Chair and Vice Chair for 2026-2027, and discussed meeting topics for the coming year.
keyTopics: Swearing-in of incoming 2026-2028 Teen Commissioners
Teen Commission orientation for new members
Presentation on teen programs
Selection of 2026-2027 Chair and Vice Chair
Discussion of Teen Commission meeting topics for 2026-2027

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council considered an appeal of an approved architectural review permit for a project at Civic Center Drive and Alviso Street that would demolish existing buildings and construct 14 townhomes and a duplex building with commercial space. The Council also considered a vesting tentative subdivision map for a 147-unit residential project with one commercial building at Homestead Road, processed under state housing law (SB 330). The meeting also included interviews and appointments to the Civil Service Commission.
keyTopics: Appeal of an architectural review permit approval for a 14-townhome and duplex development with commercial space at 860/858 Civic Center Drive and 1526 Alviso Street
CEQA statutory exemption determination for the Civic Center Drive/Alviso Street project under AB 130
Vesting tentative subdivision map for a 147-unit housing project with a commercial building at 3521 and 3591 Homestead Road, subject to SB 330
CEQA determination that the Homestead Road subdivision map falls within the scope of a previously adopted Mitigated Negative Declaration
Interviews and appointment of two applicants to the Civil Service Commission

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 1, 2026
milpitas.summary: This meeting was held in the City Council's role as the Successor Agency Board, handling leftover business from Milpitas's former redevelopment agency. The board considered formally confirming which city officials serve as agency officers, and considered authorizing the sale of 2026 Tax Allocation Refunding Bonds to refinance existing redevelopment-related debt.
keyTopics: Confirming and designating city officials as officers of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency
Authorizing issuance and sale of 2026 Tax Allocation Refunding Bonds to refinance Successor Agency debt

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee — September 4, 2026
palo-alto.summary: Palo Alto's Climate Action and Sustainability Committee took a preliminary look at the city's 2025 greenhouse gas inventory, including a rundown of Scope 3 emissions (indirect emissions from things like purchased goods and commuting). The committee also reviewed different approaches the city could take to reach its carbon neutrality goal and gave feedback on which areas staff should study further.
keyTopics: Preliminary review of the 2025 greenhouse gas inventory
Overview of Scope 3 emissions
Approaches to achieving the city's carbon neutrality goal
Committee feedback on areas for further staff analysis
